## F05 Sandbox and network isolation

- F05.os-sandbox — OS or container sandbox [supported, unverified] Each user's work runs in a dedicated Firecracker microVM with hardware-level separation from other users, with its own kernel, memory, and virtual devices. The computer belongs to the account, not to an individual Bot, so anything on it is available to every Bot. Grok Bot runs only on Cursor-hosted cloud computers. | ev: E-grok-bot-00034, E-grok-bot-00190, E-grok-bot-00016, E-grok-bot-00239
- F05.fs-write-scope — Filesystem write scope [supported, unverified] The computer has a shared workspace at `/workspace` for durable project files in clear project folders. Files, browser state, and supported sign-ins survive normal computer updates and recovery. | ev: E-grok-bot-00489
- F05.network-policy — Network policy [partial, verified] Blocking a plugin doesn't block that service's website; closing that path takes Network Controls (Enterprise only). Grok Bot computers reach the internet through shared static egress IP addresses. The Allow Local Egress switch is on by default and lets members route web traffic through their own computer; routed traffic is subject to that device's gateway policy. | limit: Closing that second path takes Network Controls, which is Enterprise only. | ev: E-grok-bot-00487, E-grok-bot-00316, E-grok-bot-00051, E-grok-bot-00361

- F14.concurrency-caps — Concurrency caps [supported, verified] Each Bot gets its own screen, so several Bots can use browser and desktop tools in parallel, with one computer-use task per screen at a time. Only one bulk computer operation can run per team at a time, and the API and the dashboard share that limit. | ev: E-grok-bot-00479, E-grok-bot-00260, E-grok-bot-00242, E-grok-bot-00262
- F14.parallel-subagents — Parallel subagents [partial, verified] Bots can run in parallel, message each other, share context in group chats and pass ownership of a task. Each Bot gets its own screen, so several Bots can use browser and desktop tools in parallel. | limit: one computer-use task per screen at a time | ev: E-grok-bot-00235, E-grok-bot-00478
- F14.total-agent-caps — Total agent caps [partial, verified] Starting a group chat takes a selection of two to six Bots. | limit: In New chat, select two to six Bots. | ev: E-grok-bot-00744
- F14.multi-session-coordination — Multi-session coordination [partial, verified] Your Bots can run in parallel, message each other, share context in group chats, and pass ownership of a task. One persistent Firecracker microVM per user is shared by every Bot that user runs, and Bots can read files other Bots save in `/workspace`. | limit: A group chat can add a teammate's published Team Bot, but not alongside Bots that run on your own computer. | ev: E-grok-bot-00235, E-grok-bot-00039, E-grok-bot-00822, E-grok-bot-00565

## F15 Background, scheduled and cloud-delegated work

- F15.background-tasks — Background tasks [partial, verified] Bots work from a persistent cloud computer with a browser, command line and filesystem, and work continues while the laptop is closed. Reconnecting and Recover usually take a few minutes, and Continue in Background is offered. | limit: Approvals from work that started without you, like a routine or a message from another Bot, expire after about 10 minutes. | ev: E-grok-bot-00476, E-grok-bot-00864, E-grok-bot-00502, E-grok-bot-00560
- F15.scheduled-routines — Scheduled routines [supported, unverified] A routine tells one Bot when to run a workflow. It can run on a schedule, or when something happens. Routines run in the cloud while your laptop is closed. A Timezone setting is what routines use for schedules, and a nightly research routine is given as an example. | ev: E-grok-bot-00623, E-grok-bot-00171, E-grok-bot-00460
- F15.cloud-agents — Cloud agents [supported, verified] Grok Bot is a computer-use agent that runs in Cursor's cloud, and each user's work executes on a dedicated cloud computer. Each Bot works on a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal. It runs only on Cursor-hosted cloud computers; on-premises and bring-your-own-image deployment are not supported today. | ev: E-grok-bot-00033, E-grok-bot-00230, E-grok-bot-00414
- F15.remote-sessions — Remote sessions [supported, unverified] From your phone you can message Bots, watch and take over the computer, approve actions, and pause or resume routines. Click the computer preview in the right-hand panel of a conversation to watch clicks, typing, navigation, and current status; closing the app doesn't stop cloud work. | ev: E-grok-bot-00300, E-grok-bot-00481
- F15.event-triggers — Event triggers [supported, unverified] A routine can run when something happens, such as a Slack message, a GitHub, Linear, Sentry, or PagerDuty event, an email, or a webhook call. Cursor account integrations can also start a routine from an event, and they are separate from the Slack or GitHub plugins. | ev: E-grok-bot-00623, E-grok-bot-00072, E-grok-bot-00998
- F15.delegation — Delegation to other agents [supported, verified] Grok Bot can delegate coding tasks to separate computers under your existing Cloud Agent controls. Admins can disable spawning; the switch applies to the whole team and is on by default. A Bot can also send an asynchronous message to another Bot, which wakes, handles the request, and can reply later. | ev: E-grok-bot-00041, E-grok-bot-00046, E-grok-bot-00066

## F20 Version, release channel, update path

- F20.version-at-retrieval — Version at retrieval [supported, unverified] The account menu shows the installed version. Choosing About shows Version, and Copy version info copies the version, release track, and OS. In the release feed, the commitSha field names the build the release comes from, and Linux download URLs include it. | ev: E-grok-bot-00580, E-grok-bot-00283, E-grok-bot-00276, E-grok-bot-00029
- F20.release-channels — Release channels [supported, verified] Each platform has a JSON feed at `https://api2.cursor.sh/updates/api/download/stable/{platform}/sand`. Linux builds publish with every stable release. Copy version info copies the version, release track, and OS. | ev: E-grok-bot-00275, E-grok-bot-00825, E-grok-bot-00580
- F20.update-mechanism — Update mechanism [supported, unverified] The desktop app checks for updates on its own; when one is ready the account menu shows New update available, then Install and Restart to update. Check for Updates and Restart to Update update the desktop app. The app and the computer update separately. A versioned installer can be downloaded and pushed, with the timing of the move to a new release decided. | ev: E-grok-bot-00581, E-grok-bot-00423, E-grok-bot-00490, E-grok-bot-00270
- F20.changelog-source — Changelog source [supported, unverified] Product changes are listed on the changelog at https://cursor.com/changelog. Phone updates come from the App Store or Google Play. | ev: E-grok-bot-00583
- F20.deprecation-policy — Deprecation policy [partial, verified] When Cursor stops supporting a build, the app covers its whole window with Update required until the member updates. A build loses support when it falls below Cursor's minimum version, or when it passes a maximum age and a newer release is available. Grok Bot requires an update when a version is more than 14 days old and a newer version is out. | limit: Cursor doesn't publish how long older installers stay available for download, and a pinned build works only until Cursor stops supporting it. | ev: E-grok-bot-00287, E-grok-bot-00584, E-grok-bot-00282

## F21 Relationship to host platform

- F21.host-platform — Host platform [supported, verified] Grok Bot runs only on Cursor-hosted cloud computers, and the computers Bots work on run in Cursor's cloud. On-premises deployment, deployment inside your own perimeter, and bring-your-own-image deployment are not supported today. | ev: E-grok-bot-00414, E-grok-bot-00247, E-grok-bot-00016, E-grok-bot-00966
- F21.shared-account-billing — Shared account and billing [supported, verified] Grok Bot uses your Cursor account. There is no separate Grok Bot login. Access is included on every paid individual Cursor plan and on Cursor Teams, and usage can also be granted by linking an individual SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, or X Premium+ subscription. | ev: E-grok-bot-00646, E-grok-bot-00612, E-grok-bot-00649

## F22 Usage, cost, limits and observability

- F22.usage-visibility — Usage and cost visibility [supported, verified] Usage & Billing shows weekly included usage and on-demand usage for eligible accounts, and the account menu can show weekly usage at a glance. Spend and usage are on the dashboard usage page, broken down by product. Usage analytics show the model that served each request, including failovers. | ev: E-grok-bot-00421, E-grok-bot-00010, E-grok-bot-00024
- F22.budget-caps — Budgets and caps [partial, verified] An on-demand cap can be set in Grok Bot under Settings › On-demand monthly limit, or on the web at cursor.com/dashboard › Spending › Monthly Limit. Extra usage after Weekly usage runs out is billed through Cursor and counts toward the On-demand monthly limit. | limit: A separate Grok Bot spend cap is not available today. The cap does not stop a Bot in the middle of a run, so a running task can go a little past it. | ev: E-grok-bot-00552, E-grok-bot-00455, E-grok-bot-00614
- F22.rate-limits — Rate-limit behaviour [supported, unverified] Paid Grok Bot access includes Weekly usage, which resets weekly. When it runs out, extra usage can continue as On-demand usage if on-demand is enabled. If on-demand is off, Grok Bot stops when weekly usage runs out, and the screen says you have reached your Grok Bot usage limit. | ev: E-grok-bot-00622, E-grok-bot-00614, E-grok-bot-00550
- F22.telemetry-otel — Telemetry and OpenTelemetry [partial, verified] OpenTelemetry Export streams Cursor usage metrics and logs, including recorded Grok Bot actions, to a collector you run, configured under Team Settings › OpenTelemetry Export. When configured, Action Recording events are sent to your collector tagged `cursor.surface=grok_bot`. | limit: OpenTelemetry Export is Enterprise only. | ev: E-grok-bot-00062, E-grok-bot-00397, E-grok-bot-00013
- F22.logs-debug — Logs and debug output [partial, verified] When a team enables Action Recording, Cursor records Bot actions, including scrubbed shell commands, in an internal store with a 90 day retention. In-app errors appear above the composer under Notifications; some include Copy request ID for support. Right-click a message and choose Copy request ID. | limit: Action Recording is a setting on the Grok Bot page, off by default. Action Recording events don't appear on the Audit Log page. | ev: E-grok-bot-00399, E-grok-bot-00432, E-grok-bot-00579
- F22.status-display — Status line and display [supported, unverified] The sidebar distinguishes Bots that need attention (a question, approval, or handoff), unread activity (a new result), and working status. Turning on Notifications in a Bot's settings gives a system or mobile notification when that Bot finishes or needs input. | ev: E-grok-bot-00428, E-grok-bot-00982, E-grok-bot-00429
